issue.title: Destructive-command guard false positive: redirects and quoted mentions of /dev/null flagged as destroying a protected path

steps: Create file.txt containing hello and notes.md containing TODO. Keep all fixtures in the current workspace.
Run exactly this bash command and show its actual result: cat file.txt >/dev/null 2>&1
expected: A read-only command or discard-device redirect is not classified as catastrophic deletion.
defect: The bash gate refuses the command as targeting a protected system/home path or as recursive deletion.
Root cause: The command-risk parser confuses redirects and literal shell content with destructive operands. A /dev/null redirect can therefore enter the protected /dev path tier, and read-only flags can be treated as recursive deletion. Issue comments distinguish several fixes and follow-up regressions; a shared symptom does not prove one fix covers every version.
